chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Ubaydi, from 'Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Ansari, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'A man has dirhams owed to me by another, and he gives me a kohl (eye cosmetic) [in payment].' He said: 'Silver for silver, and whatever is of kohl is a debt upon him which he will repay on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.الْفِضَّةُ بِالْفِضَّةِ: Silver for silver (a principle of equal value for same-kind currency)
key_terms.مُكْحُلَةً: A kohl (eye cosmetic), used here as a commodity for debt repayment

ai.seo_question: How is a debt repaid with a different commodity treated in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that repaying a silver debt with kohl constitutes a transfer of value where the kohl itself becomes a distinct debt owed by the debtor to the creditor. This ruling underscores the principle of *qard bi al-qard* (debt for debt) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the commodity given is not merely a substitute payment but a new liability that must be settled, highlighting the spiritual weight of financial obligations. The narration serves as a practical guide for ensuring debts are cleared in a manner that satisfies both legal and eschatological justice.
